description:
## Outcome

One lifecycle policy defines admission, active work, client disconnects, drain, cancel, deadlines, forced stop, and cleanup. The daemon and protocol implementation enforce that policy.

## Work

1. Define idle, accepting, draining, cancelling, stopping, and stopped states.
2. State when a disconnected client cancels work and when durable work continues.
3. Stop new admission when shutdown starts.
4. Define drain and cancellation deadlines, forced-stop behavior, and terminal event order.
5. Preserve the primary work error and each cleanup error without secret data.
6. Close listeners, sessions, stores, and discovery ownership in a fixed order.
7. Add injected clock and cancellation boundaries and document service-manager expectations.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Idle and active shutdown have deterministic state transitions.
- [ ] No new request starts after draining begins.
- [ ] Blocked work receives public Jidoka cancellation before forced stop.
- [ ] Each accepted request has one terminal result or one explicit interrupted-state record.
- [ ] Cleanup runs after success, error, cancellation, disconnect, and deadline.
- [ ] Repeated stop requests are safe and idempotent.

## Tests

Add lifecycle state-machine, race, blocked-work, disconnect, timeout, cancellation-failure, and cleanup-failure tests. Run `mix quality`, `mix test --cover`, and `mix docs`.

## Non-goals

Do not define an OS service wrapper. Do not add hot upgrades or distributed work.
title: Define and enforce the daemon work lifecycle and shutdown policy
